newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary K&H bank sale sees 17 potential bidders.
newsitem.headline: Hungary K&H bank sale sees 17 potential bidders.

text.p: Seventeen international investors have expressed interest in the privatisation of Kereskedelmi Bank Rt (K&H), Hungary's third largest bank in terms of assets, K&H said on Wednesday.
The information memorandum of the bank, which Hungary plans to privatise fully by the end of next year, was sent to 72 potential investors, K&H chief executive Janos Eros told a news conference.
"Seventeen investors expressed their inclination to do due diligence at the bank," Eros said.

The state privatisation agency APV said earlier that it would publish a closed two-round tender for the sale to a strategic investor of an at least 25 percent plus one vote stake in K&H, by January 15.
The investor should acquire the stake through buying shares and increasing the bank's capital.
APV added it would also publish a tender by March 1 for financial investors to raise the registered capital of K&H, which currently stands at 10.3 billion forints ($62.8 million), by $40 million.
Eros said the bank would need a capital increase of at least five billion forints. However, he believes the capital will be raised by 10 to 15 billion forints during the privatisation.
The fresh capital would enable K&H to launch new products and continue to develop its integrated computer network and connect all its branches with its on-line operation system.
K&H has 180 branches, which is the second largest network in Hungary, but the number of branches is likely to be reduced to some 140, Eros said.
The bank projects that its balance sheet total will increase to 356 billion forints in 1996 and 380 to 382 billion in 1997 from 326 billion in 1995, he said.
He added the after-tax profits were seen increasing to 2.2 billion forints in 1996 and some three billion in 1997 from 1.9 billion forints in 1995.
The figures were calculated according to Hungarian accounting standards.

The bank substantially improved its credit portfolio in the past three years as its risky loans amounted to 9.3 percent of all claims in 1995, and this rate was likely to drop to 6.3 percent in 1996 and to below five percent in 1997, Eros said.

The price of K&H shares on the OTC market has risen to 110 to 115 percent of the face value from 15 to 20 percent in mid-1995, he said, adding that the recent privatisation of another large bank, MHB, substantially contributed to the firming of K&H shares.
Dutch ABN AMRO bought an 89.23 percent stake in MHB for $89.23 million last month.
K&H is the last large Hungarian bank to be privatised.
